scholarships.title: Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation PhD Scholarship (2027 competition)

eligibility: At the time of application the applicant must be in the first year or the second year of a PhD program.
The field of study must be broadly related to the humanities or social sciences and address issues relevant to Canada's future.
The PhD research must align with at least one of the Foundation's four themes: Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment.

The applicant must be one of the following: a Canadian student enrolled at a Canadian university; a Canadian student enrolled at a university outside Canada; or an international student enrolled at a Canadian university.
Applicants must demonstrate outstanding academic achievement and a high level of intellectual ability, assessed across the whole application including transcripts and letters of recommendation.
Three letters of reference are required: one from the PhD supervisor, one from another academic referee, and one from a referee outside academia.
There is no age limit to apply.
There is no requirement to be fluent in both official languages; applicants must be able to communicate effectively in either French or English.
existing.eligibility_summary: Doctoral students in the first or second year of a PhD at the time of application whose research is broadly humanities/social sciences and aligns with at least one of the Foundation's four themes, who are either a Canadian student enrolled at a Canadian university, a Canadian student enrolled at a university outside Canada, or an international student enrolled at a Canadian university.
benefits: Annual stipend of up to $50,000 for three years to cover tuition and living expenses related to doctoral studies
Annual allowance of up to $20,000 for three years to support research, networking activities, and travel related to the doctoral work
Membership in the Foundation's community of Scholars, Fellows and Mentors
Lifelong membership in the Foundation's alumni network of more than 500 individuals
Mentorship and experiential learning: meetings, masterclasses, seminars and field experiences

Applications that do not meet the eligibility criteria will not be reviewed
Provide exactly three letters of reference — thesis supervisor, another academic referee, and a non-academic referee — no more and no fewer

The application form must be filled out in one language only, either English or French
Attend the mandatory information sessions offered in the weeks of October 5 and October 12, 2026

Special Circumstances section explanation, if a former supervisor or another professor must act as PhD supervisor referee
existing.english_requirement: Applicants must be able to communicate effectively in either French or English. The Foundation states: "Do I need to be fluent in both French and English to receive the scholarship? No. You do not need to be fluent in both official languages. However, you must be able to communicate effectively in either French or English." The application form may be completed in English or French, in one language only, and referees may respond in either language regardless of the language of the application.
application_method: Read the published eligibility criteria and confirm your profile meets all requirements.
Complete the short eligibility screening form on the SmartSimple portal (https://fdnpetf.smartsimple.ca) by October 2, 2026.
Wait for the Foundation to confirm eligibility and grant access to the full application form.
Attend a mandatory information session in the week of October 5 or October 12, 2026.
Complete the full application form, including the research proposal and the Special Circumstances section where relevant.
Nominate your three referees within the application file so they receive access to the letter instructions; referees must submit their letters by October 30, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET.
Submit the complete application by November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET.
Receive a confirmation email acknowledging submission once your application is received.
existing.selection_notes: Applications are assessed on academic excellence, the clear alignment of the research project with the Foundation's mission and four founding themes, the rigour of the research proposal, and the ability to share knowledge for the benefit of society. Only applications meeting the programme's eligibility criteria are assessed. Applicants who pass review are notified by email; all other applicants are informed at the end of the application review period. Applicants shortlisted in the selection process are invited to group meetings and individual interviews, conducted in French or English depending on the applicant's preference. Final decisions are approved by the Board of Directors. The application form is removed from the portal once the competition ends; the confirmation email is the only proof of receipt.
existing.best_fit: First- or second-year PhD students in the humanities and social sciences whose research maps onto one of the Foundation's four themes (Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment), who already have an outstanding academic record and who want mentorship and a non-academic network alongside funding.
existing.notes: The Scholarship is a three-year program. It is not deferrable in the sense that the value is adjusted: Scholars may accept other awards, but the value of the Trudeau Scholarship is adjusted based on amounts received from other organizations, institutions or universities, and all additional sources of income must be declared annually. Regardless of other funding, every Scholar receives the full annual $20,000 research, travel and networking allowance and a minimum of $25,000 from the annual stipend. For Scholars studying outside Canada who receive external funding in foreign currency, the Foundation converts that amount into Canadian dollars; the location of study does not affect the Scholarship amount. Scholars may work part-time (up to 20 hours per week) while continuing to receive full benefits, including university or campus-based roles such as research assistant, teaching assistant or lecturer. Scholars may suspend the Scholarship for up to one year for parental, medical, personal or professional leave; the Foundation states Scholars are not employees of the Foundation and it does not provide paid parental leave, and payments are paused until the Scholar re-enrols full-time. Funds begin only after Board of Directors approval, signature of the funding agreement and submission of required documentation. The annual Scholarship is disbursed in three instalments per year. There is no return-home requirement for Canadian students studying abroad or for international students.
existing.application_period: Applications open September 1, 2026 and close November 6, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. ET. Two-step process: eligibility verification form must be submitted by October 2, 2026; references received by October 30, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET; mandatory information sessions in the weeks of October 5 and October 12, 2026.
existing.deadline_display: November 6, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. ET (deadline to submit the complete application); October 2, 2026 (deadline to request eligibility confirmation); October 30, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. ET (deadline for receipt of all three references)
